title: capacity-symphony-hiring-vs-price-sensitivity-notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working workbook for aligning short-term hiring with slab/price moves and demand shocks. This is intentionally rough — a finance + infra playbook to decide: when do we hire, when do we tolerate higher spot spend, and how low can published prices go before HC or slab commitments must shift.

TL;DR:
- If published price per 1M tokens drops below $6.50 on average (across embeddings + gen mix), we should delay non-critical hires for 8–12 weeks or flip to a temporary burst-reserve (paying ~15% premium) until clear demand materializes.
- For a 25% demand spike sustained >6 weeks, recommended short-term response: 1) enable burst-reserve, 2) pull forward 6 FTEs from contractor-to-hire pipeline (4 infra ops, 2 SRE), 3) run a 4-week micro-rollout of quantization profiles on non-enterprise customers to recover unit margins.

Key assumptions (base case):
- Avg tokens per request (gen): 1.2k
- Gen/embedding mix: 70% gen, 30% embeddings by spend
- Avg gross margin target: 55% at published price $8/1M tokens
- Avg infra cost per 1M tokens (gpu+network+storage): $2.45 (baseline, optimized batching + prefix cache)
- Average fully-burdened engineer cost (on-roll): $240k/year (~$20k/month)
- Median time-to-productivity for infra hires: 10 weeks

Scenario matrix (monthlyized snapshot; $k):
CSV format for paste into quick sheets
scenario,net-new-hires,contractor-pulls,expected-net-hc,monthly-salary-runrate,monthly-infra-ops-budget,token-costs(1M),published-price(1M),expected-margin
base,0,0,312,5200,850,2.45,8.00,57%
price-compression,-6,0,306,5080,820,2.45,6.20,40%
demand-spike,8,6,326,5720,980,2.88,8.00,47%
burst-reserve-mode,0,12,324,5340,1200,2.45,8.00,52%
quantization-pilot,0,0,312,5200,720,1.90,8.00,61%

Notes on above numbers:
- "monthly-infra-ops-budget" includes GPU rental, spot/commit blending, and expected burst premiums.
- token-costs(1M) in demand-spike assumes 18% increase due to more short-lived small batches; quantization-pilot reduces cost by ~22% in pilot segments.

Headcount phasing (quarterly view):
- Q1 2026: +4 infra engineers (contractor conversion), +2 SRE (on contract ramp), delay 3 product hires to Q2 if price compression scenario triggers.
- Q2 2026: Conditional +8 hires if demand-spike persists >6 weeks; otherwise scale back to +2 (ops automation).
- Hiring prioritization: infra (40%), SRE (25%), product (20%), CS/Support (15%).

Pricing sensitivity test (simple marginal model):
- Compute breakeven price per 1M tokens given different HC scenarios. Formula (simplified): breakeven = (infra_unit_cost + additional_salary_impact_per_1M_tokens) / (1 - target_margin)
- Example calculations (rounded):
  * With 10 FTE added (annual cost $2.4M) and expected 12M additional 1M-token-equivalents/month, additional salary impact = ($2.4M/12)/1M = $0.20 per 1M tokens. breakeven @ target 55% = (2.45 + 0.20)/(0.45) = $5.0 -> implies published price needs floor ~ $5.0 (but we keep buffer to $6.5).

Sensitivity grid (short extract):
- If published price falls to $6.20: margin compression -> freeze non-critical hiring; trigger burst reserve acceptance for up to 10% of peak demand.
- If published price rises to $9.00: accelerate contractor-to-full-hire conversions, add +12 FTEs across infra/product.
- If infra unit cost increases by 15% (spot market): re-run quantization pilot across 20% of traffic within 14 days.

Actionable playbook (operational):
- Price monitoring: finance to ingest daily published price signals and take action if 7-day MA < $6.75. (Owner: Sofia)
- Hiring hold threshold: if 3-week trailing margin < 48% and expected price < $6.5 within next 8 weeks, freeze non-critical roles. (Owner: People Ops + Finance)
- Burst-reserve runbook: on-call infra lead to execute burst-reserve allocation, cap at 12% of baseline capacity for first 2 weeks, escalate to execs if needed. (Owner: SRE)
- Quantization gate: product + applied-ml run stair-step rollout (5% -> 20% -> 50%) with automated quality checks tied to eval harness. Rollback window 48h. (Owner: Applied ML)

Open questions & risks (notes-to-self):
- How correlated is price compression to demand vs aggressive competitor price cuts? If competitor-driven, we may accept margin erosion temporarily to preserve volume; if demand-driven, we should tighten capacity. Need further market intel.
- Contractual implications for Dedicated customers if we reduce burst capacity pricing. Legal to review.
- Operational risk: rapid contractor conversions may increase turnover; plan for mentorship budget.

Mini-checklist before exec review (2/20/2026):
- [ ] Validate 3rd-party spot forecasts with infra (Liam)
- [ ] Run quick scenario where quantization saves only 10% (worse-case) and confirm runway impact (Priya)
- [ ] Prepare 1-pager for revenue ops on hold thresholds and customer communication draft (Sofia)

Appendix (quick references):
- Short-term forecast assumptions: conservative demand growth 6% MoM baseline, volatility band +-18%
- Rapid takeaway: keep a $1.5/month per-engineer buffer in the model for training/onboarding churn for the first 3 months post-hire.
- Last run of similar playbook: Oct 2025 during GPU spot spike; outcome: used burst-reserve for 3 weeks, converted 5 contractors, preserved service levels.

Questions for next meeting (finance + infra):
1) Can infra generate a tighter per-token cost estimate if we limit trace-length to 700 tokens for non-verified requests? (Owner: Liam)
2) How fast can we turn on per-customer quant profiles in Redwood Optimize to target the worst 10% of token-heavy customers? (Owner: Applied ML)
3) Is there an ops automation that can shorten median time-to-productivity from 10->7 weeks for infra hires? (Owner: People Ops)

Notes: keep this doc informal. We'll iterate numbers into the canonical sheet once the above validations complete.
